profile.commute: a 2009 Volvo V70 wagon with a roof rack
profile.hobby: collecting sea glass at Higgins Beach

memories.text: Went down to Higgins Beach at low tide and found one piece of cobalt blue sea glass, which is the first blue I have found since April.
The sea glass lives in three mason jars on the kitchen sill sorted by colour, and the green jar is so full the lid no longer sits flat.
Decided to open the year with the copper cycle lab instead of flame tests, because the flame tests always burn the whole first week on one afternoon of colour.
Fennel stole a wool sock off the drying rack and buried it in the raised bed, and I only found it because the corner was sticking out of the soil.
I have three sections of AP chemistry this year and eighty-four students on the rosters, which is eleven more than last year.
Inventoried the stockroom and found the silver nitrate bottle down to about a fifth, so I put in the order before the district freezes purchasing.
Drove the Volvo out to Bradbury Mountain with Fennel and did the loop in an hour and ten, which is slower than usual because of the blackflies.
My twin nieces Juno and Wren video called to show me a jar of pond water and demanded I identify everything swimming in it.
Decided to build the cold frame out of the old storm windows in the garage rather than buy the kit, and cut the first two cedar rails to forty-eight inches.
I drink Earl Grey with a splash of oat milk, and I have never once finished a mug before it goes cold on the windowsill.
The new principal, Mr. Alvarado, asked me to take on the science fair coordinator role and I said I would only do it if I get the big lab on Fridays.
The fume hood alarm went off during the walkthrough and the maintenance lead traced it to a sash sensor that had been taped over since last spring.
Decided to seat the classes in groups of four rather than pairs, and drew the whole seating chart on graph paper with a mechanical pencil.
Laminated ninety-six element cards for the periodic table game and the laminator jammed twice on the lanthanides.
My neighbour Doris came over the fence to say she would take Fennel on her afternoon walks once school starts, and refused to be paid for it.
The Volvo's check engine light came on at the Forest Avenue lights and went off again by the time I parked, which is the fourth time this summer.
First day with students is the twenty-sixth, and my first period starts at seven forty-five with the section that has nineteen seniors in it.
Decided the phone policy this year is a hanging shoe rack by the door, numbered one through thirty, and no exceptions for the seniors.
